text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page triggered -> rotation 'oncall-prod'
incident-bot: ALERT: latency.slo.p99 > 3.0s (5m). Service: model-serving-prod (east-1). p99=4.6s, p95=1.2s. Link: https://dash.redwood/internal/alerts/INC-7289
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: page fired (INC-7289). Escalation timer: 10m. Notified: @oncall-prod
Priya: oncall here, acking the page :wave: I'm taking first look. grabbing logs + tail metrics.
Liam: I see correlated KV eviction spikes on the hotkey shard + increased request fanout. stack: kv-cache -> sidecar -> runtime. evictions/sec jumped x12 around the spike.
Miguel: can we do a quick mitigation: (1) scale dedicated-pool-prod-east +2, (2) remove cross-region fallback for a minute, or (3) flip traffic to model-compact-1 for non-critical customers?
Priya: doing #1 now. running: ```redwoodctl pool scale --pool dedicated-prod-east --delta 2 --reason "p99 spike INC-7289"``` will also check queue depths.
Beth: I can temporarily disable continuous batching for the hotpath route to reduce head-of-line blocking. patching route config now.
Priya: Beth, go for it. paste the small patch here when ready.
Beth: patch: ```route-config {
  name: /v1/generate/hotpath
  batching: { enabled: false }
}``` applied to canary. monitoring.
incident-bot: autoscaler triggered: added 2 nodes to dedicated-prod-east (node-group dpe-01). Expected warmup ~45s.
Liam: quick log snippet: ```[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] kv: eviction key=hot:user:1234 size=8MB. free_mem=12%```
Miguel: sidecar queue latency was the main contributor. disabling batching should cut queue time by ~300-600ms.
Priya: p99 dropped from 4.6s -> 3.1s after nodes joined; still above SLO. continuing mitigation.
Aisha-CS: tagging CS: heads-up that some EU customers routed via east-1 may see higher latency. I'll send a brief note if we expect >15m impact.
Liam: opened a temporary KV pin for top 5 hotkeys: ```kvctl pin --key hot:user:1234 --ttl 60m``` reduces eviction churn.
Priya: good. Also temporarily routing heavy customers to fallback-dedicated-2 to isolate noisy tenants.
Miguel: observed GPU utilization flat. this is more cache / queueing than GPU saturation. Good sign.
Priya: monitoring p95/p99 and SLO burn window. current: p99=2.9s, p95=0.95s, SLO window still flagged but trending down.
Beth: re-enabled small batching on canary with lower batch size to balance throughput. config: batching.max_tokens=256, max_batch_wait_ms=8
Priya: handover: I need to step off rotation in 28m. handing to Liam for follow-ups and post-incident write-up. Liam, can you take the active owner?
Liam: ack. I'll keep watches and coordinate with infra to tighten autoscaler hysteresis and review KV eviction thresholds.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: reminder: INC-7289 auto-escalation suppressed (ack received). If unacked for 9m, escalate to SRE Lead.
Miguel: current metrics: p99 back under SLO for 10m sample window. I'll keep an eye on tail spikes, but looks stabilized.
Priya: nice job team. quick notes for postmortem: root cause likely KV cache thrash from hotkey fanout + too-aggressive batching on hotpath. Mitigations we applied: scale dedicated pool, disable batching on hotpath, pin hotkeys, route noisy tenants to fallback pool.
Aisha-CS: CS updated: sent proactive email to impacted customers in EU explaining short latency blip and actions taken. No SLA credits expected at this time.
Liam: creating follow-up ticket for infra: adjust autoscaler config and add eviction alert to SLO runbook. I'll also collect heap profiles and KV metrics for next 24h.
Priya: closing page thread here. If SLO burn exceeds 30m we'll open a full incident and schedule postmortem meeting.
incident-bot: Incident INC-7289: p99 latency returned below threshold (3.0s) for 15m. Auto-close scheduled in 30m.
Priya: thread closed for now. thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
